doc.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024

chapter: Learning jazz and finding Latin music
title: Learning by osmosis, then Andy Gonzalez and Latin identity
summary: He learned by listening to Bud Powell and hanging out with elders; years later Andy Gonzalez told him to embrace Latin music. Monk Rowe comments on how hard Latin music is to grasp.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: how was that?” And then they would give you information. But it was our osmosis. You’d learn to be a jazz musician by (a) listening intently — I was a Bud Powell freak — I listened to nothing but Bud Powell, and then just by osmosis, hanging out with those older jazz musicians, and then of course we would play any gig we could get. So that was about the age of 16 was that part of my life. And I didn’t embrace anything remotely Latin ‘til years later when I met to the great bassist Andy Gonzalez and he told me that it was important for me to embrace the entry point of my people into the conversation we call jazz.

I think that when I listen — of course pan-Latin music — I’ve had a lot of trouble knowing where I am. And I’ve used this excuse with me that oh this music you really need to have lived when you were a kid. You need to hear it from the time you’re a child to really embrace it. And it’s probably not true.
